items.question: What is WJP full-color 3D printing?
items.answer: WJP (Wax Jet Printing) is an industrial-grade full-color 3D printing process using wax-jet + curing. It directly prints 16-million-color models with no post-processing coloring needed. High color fidelity and fine texture — perfect for portraits, pets, anime characters, and any scene that needs color and detail preserved.

items.question: Can I really order just one piece? Any minimum?
items.answer: Absolutely. One-piece minimum, no MOQ. Our production line is purpose-built for single-piece / small-batch customization — every order handled individually from start to finish. Bulk orders (30+) enjoy group pricing — see the Pricing page.

items.question: How long until I receive my order?
items.answer: Standard orders deliver in 5-7 working days (excluding remote areas). Process: 24h 3D proof → customer approval → 48-72h WJP printing → Express shipping dispatch. Rush service: contact customer support.

items.question: Is one photo enough? Do I need professional images?
items.answer: A single front photo works, but the result may be slightly less ideal. We recommend 3-5 photos from different angles (front + side + back / top). AI-generated images, illustrations, and anime reference sheets are all accepted.

items.question: What products can I order? Any size limits?
items.answer: Pet badges (~30-50mm), keychains (~40-60mm), fridge magnets (~60-100mm), figures (~100-200mm), standees (~150-300mm) all supported. For over 200mm or complex shapes, please contact customer support for evaluation.

items.question: Who owns the 3D model files?
items.answer: You do. After modeling is complete, we provide STL / OBJ files for download. You can use them for personal collection, re-printing, or commercial sublicensing. We retain no copyright and will not resell your work.

items.question: What if I'm not satisfied with the final product?
items.answer: At the 3D proof stage, one free revision; full refund if you reject the proof entirely. At the printing stage, defects (color loss, breakage, etc.) are remade free or refunded in full. Shipping damage is replaced free with packaging photos.

items.question: Which payment methods are supported? Invoices available?
items.answer: WeChat Pay, Alipay, and corporate bank transfer. Business customers can apply for VAT ordinary invoices or special invoices — contact customer support to register.

algorithm.title: How the weight is calculated
algorithm.p1: Resin weight = solid volume × material density. The solid volume comes from the model's bounding box scaled by the fill ratio; in manual mode it is estimated from the envelope size × fill ratio.
algorithm.formula: Weight = solid volume (cm³) × material density ({density} g/cm³)
algorithm.p2: Support weight is estimated from the honeycomb fill rate, the shell thickness and the support resin density; use “Support weight calibration” to back-solve it from a measured weight. The optimizer picks the pose with the least support and the lowest layer height.

thickness.thinArea: Thin areas cover {ratio}% of the surface ({count} sampled faces)
thickness.unreliable: {miss}/{total} rays hit nothing — the mesh is not closed, so treat these numbers as a rough guide.

issues.degenerateHint: Three points almost collinear, so the area is zero — slicers usually skip these or throw an error.
issues.duplicateFaceHint: The same triangle appears more than once, which shows up as a double layer on the surface.
issues.openEdgeHint: This edge is shared by only one face — the mesh is not closed and the slice will have holes.
issues.nonManifoldEdgeHint: Three or more faces share one edge — most slicers simply fail on this.
issues.duplicateVertexHint: Same coordinates but treated as different vertices, so the mesh was never welded. This usually causes the open edges.
issues.flippedNormalHint: Neighbouring faces point in opposite directions, which flips the shading and can make the computed volume negative.
issues.thinWallHint: Walls below the thin limit — 1.0-1.2mm is a reasonable floor for photo-resin.
issues.overhangHint: Faces angled more than {angle}° downwards, which need supports to print.

overhang.title: Overhangs
overhang.hint: Faces angled more than {angle}° downwards need supports — the smaller the share, the easier it prints.
